solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Genuine stunner's quite heartless

indicators.note: a thing without its heart has lost its central letter

parts.note: a knockout blow stuns, and a stunning person is a knockout
sheer can mean completely or quite, as in sheer madness

explanation.surface: A dazzling beauty turns out to be rather cold-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a possessive joining the pieces; SHEER loses one of its two middle Es to give SHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Kosher is informal for legitimate or above board, borrowed from the Jewish dietary term.

clue.text: Opener has to hit cross heavenward

indicators.note: in a down clue, going heavenward means reading from the bottom up

parts.note: to bonk is to hit on the head
a rood is a crucifix or cross

explanation.surface: A tale of someone striking a cross that points skywards, with an opener in it somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: Opener is a playful definition: a doorknob is what you grip to open a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorknob is the handle turned to open a door, so it is literally an opener.

clue.text: Chinese people's award for vehicle

parts.note: the Han are China's majority ethnic group, plus the possessive S
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A Chinese community receives a prize for building a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A hansom is a two-wheeled horse-drawn cab, a vehicle of Victorian streets.

clue.text: Remark about including agreement with clubs in meeting hall?

indicators.note: including means the first word wraps around what follows

parts.note: a comment is a remark
unity is accord or agreement
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A comment concerning a club agreement reached at a gathering in a hall.
explanation.walkthrough: About does double duty in the surface but here gives a separate piece at the end. The question mark flags that a meeting hall is just one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A community centre is a local building where residents gather for meetings and events.

clue.text: Spy a fashionable fruit

parts.note: a plant is a spy placed inside an organisation
taken as written
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone spots a trendy piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Spy looks like a verb meaning to see; it is a noun for an undercover agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A plantain is a starchy banana-like tropical fruit, usually cooked before eating.

clue.text: English icon's ultimately lacking wit

indicators.note: lacking its ultimate part means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
in computing a sprite is a small graphic image, like an icon

explanation.surface: A national hero is judged, in the end, to have no sense of humour.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit, borrowed from French, means liveliness of mind and quick humour.

clue.text: Title of letter?

parts.note: surface reading: the heading written at the top of a piece of correspondence
setter's reading: a letter is one who lets property, and the title is the legal ownership a landlord holds outright

explanation.walkthrough: Letter is not post but a landlord, one who lets; the title is a property deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright ownership of land, with no lease term, is the legal title a landlord may hold.

clue.text: Speak fondly about boy drowning men in American river

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around everything after it

parts.note: to coo is to murmur affectionately

indicators.note: to drown something is to submerge it, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: a lad is a boy
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Someone murmurs tenderly over a lad who drowned some men in a river in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: the men sink inside the boy, and the boy inside the cooing. OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword soldiery.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colorado flows through the south-western United States and carved the Grand Canyon.

clue.text: Brilliance of characters returning in Gilbert & Sullivan

indicators.note: returning means the letters are read back the other way
characters here means letters sitting in a row in the clue's own text

parts.note: the letters straddling the end of Gilbert and the start of Sullivan

explanation.surface: Praise for the dazzle of the comic-opera characters in Gilbert and Sullivan productions.
explanation.walkthrough: Characters suggests the people in the operas; it means letters. Gilbert and Sullivan wrote Victorian comic operettas.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is a gleaming sheen or shine, and figuratively glory or brilliance.

clue.text: Carves up small furry animals

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
hares are long-eared furry mammals

explanation.surface: A butcher or predator slices up little fluffy creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: To share something out is to divide it into portions, as you carve up a joint.

clue.text: Tone set by report of collier alongside jetty

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: a collier is a coal miner
a quay is a landing wharf or jetty

explanation.surface: A mood is established by an account of a coal miner standing beside a pier.
explanation.walkthrough: Report of covers both words: miner becomes MINOR and quay becomes KEY. A collier is a British word for a coal miner.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor key is a musical scale that gives a piece a sad or sombre tonality.

clue.text: Presenter's piece on weather feature

parts.note: a front is the boundary between air masses on a weather map
a man is a piece in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A TV weather presenter's segment about an approaching front.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, piece on weather feature puts MAN after FRONT. The 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontman is the person who fronts a show or band, its public host or lead figure.

clue.text: Court case involving one in London area

indicators.note: involving means wrapping around and enclosing something

parts.note: Acton is a district of west London
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lawsuit involving a single person from somewhere in London.
explanation.definitionFit: An action is a legal proceeding brought in court, a lawsuit.

clue.text: Absurd dons dealt badly with hypocrisy

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written: all fifteen letters

explanation.surface: Ridiculous university lecturers acted unfairly, showing two-faced behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: Absurd looks like it might signal the shuffle, but it is fodder; badly is the signal. Dons are Oxbridge lecturers.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying different rules to oneself and others is the essence of hypocrisy.

clue.text: Ordinary job in Gap

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level
a mission is an assigned task or job

explanation.surface: A routine job at the clothing chain Gap.
explanation.walkthrough: Gap's capital suggests the shop; it is the definition. O levels were the old British ordinary-level exams.
explanation.definitionFit: An omission is something left out, leaving a gap in a text or record.

clue.text: Standing out with some debs dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and land in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A few debutantes at a ball catch the eye on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: Debs are debutantes, upper-class young women formerly presented at society balls.
explanation.definitionFit: An embossed design is raised in relief from the surface, so it physically protrudes.

clue.text: Stagger from Birmingham area?!

parts.note: Aston is a district of Birmingham, home of Aston Villa
the question mark asks whether it is only roughly that, which the suffix ish expresses

explanation.surface: Someone lurches unsteadily out of a part of Birmingham.
explanation.walkthrough: The ?! turns Birmingham area into a tentative guess, Aston-ish, meaning something like Aston.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to amaze or stun them, the same as to astonish.

clue.text: Chemical shield covers vehicle

indicators.note: to cover something is to lie around it, enclosing it

parts.note: a bib shields clothing from food
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A chemical protective barrier is applied over a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Bicarb is short for sodium bicarbonate, a common household chemical compound.

clue.text: Azerbaijan meadow contains a flower

indicators.note: contains means the word wraps around the next item

parts.note: AZ is the international code for Azerbaijan
a lea is a poetic word for a meadow
taken as written

explanation.surface: A meadow in Azerbaijan is home to a single bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: The country code and the meadow sit side by side, and the lone a slips into the gap between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The azalea is a flowering shrub of the rhododendron family, grown for its showy blooms.

clue.text: Including drink in court, charge is nonsense

indicators.note: including means the second word wraps around the first

parts.note: CT is the abbreviation for court
to lap is to drink as a cat does
a rap is a criminal charge, as in a murder rap

explanation.surface: A defendant protests that a charge involving drinking in court is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Including comes first but acts on court, which wraps the drink; the charge then follows on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious or empty talk, rubbish meant to win applause.

clue.text: Salve regularly extracted from Aurantiaceae

indicators.note: regularly taken means every other letter is picked out at even intervals

parts.note: the first, third, fifth letters and so on

explanation.surface: An ointment is derived from a botanical family of citrus plants.
explanation.walkthrough: Aurantiaceae is an old name for the orange family of plants, which lends the surface a plausible herbal ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnica is a herbal ointment rubbed on bruises and sprains.

clue.text: Missing fish found under a stone

parts.note: taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A lost fish turns up beneath a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, fish found under a stone puts RAY below A and ST. A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone astray has wandered off and is lost, so it is absent.

clue.text: A crime involving short insolent killer

indicators.note: involving means wrapping around and enclosing something

parts.note: taken as written
a sin is a wrongdoing or crime

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, missing its final letter

parts.note: sassy means cheeky or insolent

explanation.surface: A crime committed by a cheeky young murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: The trimmed insolent word sits inside the crime just after its first letter, with the opening A placed in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a person who murders, especially a prominent figure, for hire or politics.

clue.text: Presumably cricket practice is cancelled for these groups

parts.note: something cancelled means there is none of it
cricketers practise in nets, enclosures of netting

explanation.surface: A cricket team's practice session is called off, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Nets are a British cricket term for practice in netted lanes. Presumably flags the whimsical reading of the answer as no-nets.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonets are ensembles of nine musicians or pieces written for such a group.

clue.text: Fuse together light gas in part of reactor

indicators.note: in means one item is placed inside another

parts.note: the core of a nuclear reactor holds its fuel
HE is the chemical symbol for helium, a very light gas

explanation.surface: Instructions for welding pieces with a light gas inside a nuclear reactor.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to stick or bond together into a single unified whole.

clue.text: Musician stuns sailor

parts.note: to rock someone is to shock or stun them
a tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A performer astonishes a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock star is a famous popular musician performing rock music.
